outcome: onset of delivery (spontaneous vs. iatrogenic induction)
cohort: 290 preterm singleton infants (73 <28 weeks and 217 28+0 to 33+0 weeks gestation) who received a complete course of antenatal corticosteroids within a week before birth, divided into small-for-gestational age (SGA) and non-SGA groups.
finding: A full course of antenatal corticosteroids had similar effects on most neonatal outcomes in SGA and non-SGA preterm singletons, but appeared detrimental for necrotizing enterocolitis in the SGA group.
mod_finding: Spontaneous onset of delivery was more common in non-SGA preterm neonates, while iatrogenic induction of labor prevailed with SGA neonates.
